title: Theoretical modeling for cognitive science and psychology
description: 'Welcome to this open and interactive textbook on theoretical modeling for cognitive science and psychology.' Part I Intro (Chapter 1 Introduction; Chapter 2 Conceptual foundations), Part II Formalizing (Chapter 3 Math concepts and notation; 4 Formal proofs; 5 Subset choice; 6 Coherence), Part III Simulating (Chapter 8 Simulating in Scala; 9 Scala and mathlib; 10 Subset choice). Chapter 2 covers why scientists model, explaining capacities rather than effects, Marr's computational, algorithmic and implementational levels (distinguished from levels of organisation) and the point that 'models that predict need not explain, and vice versa'.

Chapter 1 Introduction: For whom is this book?; What this book is (not) about; Approach; Tools for Theory; Scala; Further Reading. Audience: students and researchers in cognitive science or psychology, including those with little or no training in theory or modelling; not a survey of existing models and not training in a specific architecture such as ACT-R or neural networks

Chapter 2 Conceptual foundations: Why do scientists model?; Explaining capacities; Further Reading. Marr's three levels with a sorting example; 'models that predict need not explain, and vice versa' (tide-table example); 'Models that explain can be seen as answering 'why' and 'how' questions.'; capacities as primary explananda and effects as secondary
